newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan spill clean-up chief hurt in accident.
newsitem.headline: Japan spill clean-up chief hurt in accident.

text.p: The top civil servant in charge of cleanup operations for one of Japan's worst oil spills lost both his feet and an arm on Friday when he fell in front of a speeding subway train, a police spokesman said.

The spokesman told Reuters that police were mystified about how Kazuo Watanabe, 50, director of Japan's Marine Pollution and Waste Management Office, fell on to the tracks at central Tokyo's Awajicho Station.
"We know he wasn't pushed or knocked and we are interviewing people about what happened," the spokesman said.
The incident during the morning commuter period stopped trains on the busy Marunouchi Line for nearly one hour, making many people late for work.
Watanabe, whose department is in the Environment Agency ministry, was unconscious in hospital in serious condition, the spokesman added.

An Environment Agency official told Reuters that Watanabe had been working almost non-stop since January 2, when the Russian tanker Nakhodka, carrying 19,000 tonnes (133,000 barrels) of fuel oil, broke in two in stormy weather in the Sea of Japan.
Watanabe joined the Environment Agency in 1974 and took over his present post 18 months ago.
The oil spill has fouled 450 km (285 miles) of coastline, making it one of Japan's worst oil pollution accidents.
